source.stem:
A 40 W lamp wastes 34 J of energy every second by heating its surroundings.
What is the efficiency of the lamp?

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: concave mirror is the same as its neighbouring term in this chapter, so the decision does not change.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: The decision still holds even if we ignore this condition: A dental mirror uses a concave mirror to provide an enlarged image for inspection.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: This rule applies even when A dental mirror uses a concave mirror to provide an enlarged image for inspection is not true.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: Judge from the most visible feature in the figure, not from the mechanism's test.

intelligence.enrichment: Concave mirrors can provide enlarged views for close inspection and can converge light; lenses are used in devices such as eyeglasses, cameras, telescopes, microscopes, and the eye because they change how light passes through them. optical element behavior determines practical use The learner chooses concave mirrors or lenses for uses that need enlarged viewing, light concentration, or light-changing devices. Any mirror used by a doctor or in a lamp is chosen only because it reflects light, so concave shape is not important.
